knowledgeComponents.label: Generate equivalent fractions
knowledgeComponents.description: Multiply or divide numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number and explain why the value is unchanged.

knowledgeComponents.label: Read and write ratio notation
knowledgeComponents.description: Interpret a : b as a comparison of two quantities and write a ratio from a described situation.

knowledgeComponents.label: Recognise equivalent ratios
knowledgeComponents.description: Decide whether two ratios are equivalent by scaling both parts by the same factor.

knowledgeComponents.label: Find a unit rate
knowledgeComponents.description: Divide to express a rate per one unit and state the units of the result.

knowledgeComponents.label: Solve rate problems in context
knowledgeComponents.description: Use a unit rate to answer a question about a different quantity, keeping units consistent.

prerequisiteEdges.justification: Scaling both parts of a ratio is the same multiplicative move as generating an equivalent fraction, so the fraction skill has to hold first.
A learner cannot compare two ratios before reading ratio notation reliably.
A unit rate is a ratio with the second part scaled to one, so the notation comes first.
Contextual rate problems are solved by first producing a unit rate.
Checking a scaled answer against an equivalent ratio is the verification step inside a rate problem.

misconceptions.label: Adds numerators and denominators
misconceptions.description: Treats a fraction as two independent whole numbers, so 1/2 and 1/3 combine to 2/5.

misconceptions.label: Reads a part-to-part ratio as a part-to-whole fraction
misconceptions.description: Reads 2 : 3 as two thirds rather than two parts out of five.

misconceptions.label: Adds the same number to both parts of a ratio
misconceptions.description: Produces 3 : 4 from 2 : 3 by adding one to each part instead of scaling multiplicatively.

misconceptions.label: Divides in the wrong order
misconceptions.description: Computes quantity divided by cost when the question asks for cost per unit.

coursePlan.title: Ratios and rates: a three-lesson prototype unit (Year 7, sample)

units.title: Ratios and rates
units.goal: Prepare for a unit test on ratios and rates in three weeks.

lessons.title: Reading and writing ratios
lessons.objective: Write a ratio from a described situation and say what each part counts.

arc.review: Four quick equivalent-fraction items, because the class notes flagged this as shaky.
arc.modelling: Teacher writes 2 : 3 for a mix of two blue and three yellow counters and names each part aloud.
arc.guidedPractice: Six paired items where students write the ratio and then say the total, aiming for about four in five correct before release.
arc.independentPractice: Eight items mixing part-to-part and part-to-whole language.
arc.closingReview: One retrieval prompt from today and one from the fraction review.

workedExamples.prompt: A recipe uses 2 cups of oats for every 3 cups of flour. Write the ratio of oats to flour, then the fraction of the mix that is oats.
steps: Name the two quantities being compared: oats and flour.
Write them in the order asked: 2 : 3.
Add the parts to get the whole: 2 + 3 = 5.

retrievalPrompts: Without looking back, write the ratio of vowels to consonants in the word RATIO.
State one situation where 2 : 3 and 2/3 mean different things.
deepExplanatoryQuestions: Why does adding the two parts of a part-to-part ratio give the whole?

decisions.reason: Guided practice targets about four in five correct before independent work, following the master-teacher review's stated optimal success rate.

lessons.title: Equivalent ratios
lessons.objective: Decide whether two ratios are equivalent and justify the decision by scaling.

arc.review: Three ratio-notation items from lesson one, spaced two days later.
arc.modelling: Teacher scales 2 : 3 to 6 : 9 and shows why adding one to each part fails.
arc.guidedPractice: Six sorted pairs, students say equivalent or not and name the scale factor.
arc.independentPractice: Interleaved set mixing equivalence checks with notation items so the student has to decide which move applies.
arc.closingReview: One retrieval prompt naming the additive error explicitly.

steps: Find the factor from the first parts: 8 divided by 2 is 4.
Apply the same factor to the second part: 3 times 4 is 12.
Compare with the given second part: 12 matches, so the ratios are equivalent.

retrievalPrompts: Why is 3 : 4 not equivalent to 2 : 3, even though each part grew by one?
deepExplanatoryQuestions: Why does scaling both parts by the same factor leave the comparison unchanged?

decisions.reason: Independent practice mixes equivalence and notation items rather than blocking them, on the strength of a grade 7 mathematics cluster randomised trial where only the ordering changed.
Ratio notation is re-exposed two days after introduction, then again in lesson three, with the interval widening toward the test date.

lessons.title: Unit rates and rate problems
lessons.objective: Find a unit rate and use it to answer a question about a different quantity.

arc.review: Two equivalence items and one notation item, spaced from lessons one and two.
arc.modelling: Teacher works a cost-per-litre example, saying the units out loud at every step.
arc.guidedPractice: Five items where the wrong division order is the tempting move, checked before release.
arc.independentPractice: Interleaved set of rate problems and equivalence checks in AUD and metric units.
arc.closingReview: Students write the one sentence they would tell a friend who divided in the wrong order.

workedExamples.prompt: Three litres of juice cost 7.50 Australian dollars. What is the cost per litre, and what would 5 litres cost?
steps: Decide which quantity goes per one unit: cost per litre, so divide cost by litres.
Divide: 7.50 divided by 3 is 2.50 dollars per litre.
Multiply the unit rate by the new quantity: 2.50 times 5 is 12.50 dollars.
Check the units: dollars per litre times litres gives dollars.

retrievalPrompts: State the unit rate from lesson three without looking, then say its units.
deepExplanatoryQuestions: Why does checking units catch a division done in the wrong order?

decisions.reason: Every lesson opens and closes with low-stakes retrieval rather than re-reading, which is the strongest recommendation in the practice guide this scaffold cites.

evidence.quotedSpan: Use quizzes to re-expose students to key content

decisions.reason: Each worked example shows the first steps fully and leaves later steps to the learner, alternating reading a solution with solving.

evidence.quotedSpan: Interleave worked example solutions with problem-solving exercises

masteryCriteria.rule: Four of five notation items correct on two separate days.
Three consecutive equivalence items correct with a stated scale factor.
Three of four unit-rate items correct with correct units.
Two of three contextual rate problems correct, including one requiring a unit check.

decisions.reason: Lesson order is a topological order of the prerequisite graph, with equivalent fractions pulled in below stage because the learner context flagged it.
Mastery rules are stated operationally per knowledge component. No effect size is claimed for the thresholds themselves.

items.stem: A netball squad has 4 shooters and 6 defenders. What is the ratio of shooters to defenders?

options.rationale: Writes the two counts in the order named in the question.
Gives the part-to-whole fraction instead of the part-to-part ratio.
Reverses the order the question asked for.
Compares the whole squad with the defenders rather than shooters with defenders.

items.keyRationale: The question names shooters first, so the ratio is 4 : 6.

items.stem: In a mix of 2 parts cordial to 5 parts water, what fraction of the drink is cordial?

options.rationale: Adds the parts to get the whole, then writes cordial over the whole.
Uses the second part as the whole, the classic part-to-part confusion.
Gives the water fraction rather than the cordial fraction.

items.keyRationale: The whole is 2 + 5 = 7 parts, so cordial is 2/7 of the drink.

options.rationale: Adds one to each part instead of scaling multiplicatively.
Doubles the first part and adds three to the second, mixing two strategies.
Reverses the parts, which changes the comparison.

items.keyRationale: 3 times 4 is 12 and 5 times 4 is 20, so 12 : 20 is the only equivalent option.

items.stem: Four litres of paint cover 18 square metres. How many square metres does one litre cover?

options.rationale: Divides area by litres, which is the per-litre direction the question asks for.
Divides litres by area, giving litres per square metre with the wrong units.
Subtracts litres from area, treating unlike quantities as like ones.

items.keyRationale: 18 divided by 4 is 4.5 square metres per litre, and the units confirm the direction.

items.stem: Which of these is the best ratio to describe a fair share?

options.rationale: Equal parts, if fairness means equal shares.
Also equal parts, so this option is equally defensible. Two keys is why the item was rejected.

items.keyRationale: Rejected before use: 1 : 1 and 2 : 2 are both equivalent to equal shares, so the item has two defensible keys.

rejection.reason: Options A and B are equivalent ratios, so more than one option is defensible. Rejected rather than repaired.
